topic_title: Red and White Christmas Tree Ideas: 10 Ways to Style It in 2026
keyword: red and white christmas tree ideas
item_noun: red and white Christmas tree ideas
intro: Red and white is one of the easiest tree schemes to get right because the two colors already belong together through candy canes, Nordic knits and gingham. The work is in proportion. Decide whether red or white leads, then keep the other at about a third, and repeat the same shades from top to bottom. Use one red, since tomato red and burgundy side by side look like a mistake. A green tree makes red pop, while a white or flocked tree softens it into a snowy look.

picks.breed: Red and White Ball Ornament Set
picks.description: A boxed set of red and white ball ornaments is the base of almost every red and white tree, and buying one mixed set keeps the shades consistent. Look for shatterproof balls in at least three sizes and mixed finishes: shiny, matte and glitter give depth, so the tree doesn't look flat. Sets of 50 to 100 cover a six to seven-foot tree once you add ribbon and picks. Hang the largest balls first, deep inside near the trunk, then medium, then small ones at the branch tips. Check that the reds match each other in the box photo; some sets mix a bright and a darker red. Shatterproof plastic survives pets and toddlers, and you can add a few glass heirlooms higher up later.
picks.best_for: Anyone starting a red and white tree from scratch
picks.skip_if: You already own plenty of red ornaments and only need white accents
picks.quirky_fact: Placing ornaments deep in the branches as well as on the tips is what makes a tree look full from across the room.
picks.product_name: Shatterproof Christmas Ball Ornaments Set, Red and White, 70 Pieces

picks.description: Striped ribbon is the quickest way to make a tree read as red and white from a distance, because the stripes cover a lot of branch for little money. Use wired ribbon, 2.5 inches wide, so it holds loops and bends without sagging. Run it in loose vertical cascades from the top down, tucking it into the branches every 12 inches, rather than wrapping it around like a garland, which looks dated. Three to five rolls of about 10 yards each suit a seven-foot tree. Candy cane stripes look playful; a thin ticking stripe or gingham check looks more cottage. Choose one pattern for the whole tree and add plain red ribbon if you need more coverage.
picks.best_for: Filling a big tree with color quickly and cheaply
picks.skip_if: You want a quiet, minimal tree; stripes add lots of pattern
picks.quirky_fact: Wired ribbon has a thin metal wire sewn into each edge, which is why it keeps its loops.
picks.product_name: Red and White Striped Wired Christmas Ribbon 2.5 Inch x 10 Yards

picks.description: A red and white buffalo check tree skirt finishes the bottom of the tree and covers the stand, which is often the least attractive part of a set-up. The bold check repeats the tree's colors at floor level and works under a green or flocked tree. A 48-inch skirt suits most six to seven-foot trees; go bigger for wide trees so the edge shows beyond the lowest branches. Flannel and woven cotton skirts look softer and sit flat, while thin felt can wrinkle. If you want less pattern, a plain white faux fur skirt or a woven tree collar is the alternative. Buffalo check also carries over to throws and pillows nearby, which ties the tree to the room.
picks.best_for: Finishing a farmhouse or cabin-style red and white tree
picks.skip_if: Your tree already has lots of striped ribbon and pattern
picks.quirky_fact: Buffalo check is a large two-color check pattern that became popular on wool hunting shirts in North America.
picks.product_name: Red and White Buffalo Check Plaid Christmas Tree Skirt 48 Inch

picks.description: Woven paper or felt hearts in red and white are a Scandinavian tradition, and a set of them gives the tree a handmade, Nordic look rather than a shiny store look. Hang them on the branch tips among the ball ornaments, or make a whole tree of hearts, wood stars and straw ornaments for a full Nordic scheme. Felt and paper pieces are light, unbreakable and cheap, which makes them good for homes with kids and pets. They can also be a craft: woven paper hearts are folded from two strips of paper and take a few minutes each once you learn the weave. Paper pieces fade or bend over many seasons, so store them flat.
picks.best_for: Scandinavian or cottage trees and homes with small children
picks.skip_if: You want a glamorous, shiny tree; these look cozy and plain
picks.quirky_fact: Woven paper heart baskets are linked to Denmark, and Hans Christian Andersen is often credited with an early example.
picks.product_name: Scandinavian Red and White Felt Heart Christmas Ornaments Set

picks.description: A flocked tree, with white texture on the branches like fresh snow, turns red and white into a softer, wintry scheme. Red ornaments stand out sharply against the white, so you can use fewer of them and skip most white pieces. That makes it a good choice for a second tree or for anyone who wants a calmer look. Pre-lit flocked trees save the work of stringing lights through sticky branches. The trade-offs are shedding, since flocking drops white flakes during setup and takedown, and higher prices than plain trees of the same height. Lay a sheet down when you set it up, and store it in a tree bag to protect the flocking.
picks.best_for: Soft, snowy red and white looks with fewer ornaments
picks.skip_if: You dislike cleaning up white flakes or want a classic green tree
picks.quirky_fact: Flocking on artificial trees is usually a mix of fibers and adhesive sprayed on the branches.
picks.product_name: Pre-Lit Flocked Artificial Christmas Tree 7.5 ft

picks.description: Peppermint ornaments are round red and white swirls that look like the hard candy, and they bring a playful touch without changing the tree's colors. Use them as accents, about 10 to 15 on a seven-foot tree, so the tree stays classic rather than looking like a candy shop. They come in shatterproof plastic, glass and felt, and some are large enough to cluster as a tree topper. Pair them with solid red and white balls and plain ribbon, since they already carry the stripe. They suit kids' rooms and kitchen trees especially well, and they can hang on cabinet knobs or a wreath to carry the theme through the house. Plastic versions survive drops; glass ones are lovely but break easily on low branches.
picks.best_for: Family trees that want a light, playful accent
picks.skip_if: You're going for a formal or minimal Nordic look
picks.quirky_fact: The round peppermint swirl candy is sometimes called a starlight mint.
picks.product_name: Shatterproof Peppermint Candy Christmas Ornaments, Set of 12

picks.description: Red berry picks are short stems of faux berries that tuck into the branches, adding texture and natural-looking color between ornaments. Push them deep into the tree and angle them outward so the berries sit between balls rather than on top of them. About 20 to 30 picks fill out a seven-foot tree; place them in clusters of three for a fuller look. They also bridge red and white with green, which makes a red and white tree look more traditional. Choose matte berries for a natural look or glossy ones for shine, and some come frosted white, which suits a flocked tree. Keep them away from young children and pets, since loose berries can come off.
picks.best_for: Filling gaps and adding natural texture between ornaments
picks.skip_if: Small children or pets reach the low branches and might pull off berries
picks.quirky_fact: Holly berries on a real plant grow only on female trees, which need a male tree nearby.
picks.product_name: Artificial Red Berry Christmas Tree Picks, 24 Pack

picks.description: Lights set the mood of the whole tree, and warm white is the safest choice for red and white. It makes red look deep and white look creamy, while cool white can turn white ornaments bluish and red pinkish. Multicolor lights add other colors and break the scheme. Plan about 100 lights per foot of tree height for a well-lit tree. Wrap each branch from the trunk outward instead of circling the outside, which lights the ornaments from within. Thin copper or green wire fairy lights hide easily on green trees; white wire suits flocked trees. LED strings stay cool and use far less power than old incandescent ones. A plug-in timer turns them on at dusk without anyone remembering.
picks.best_for: Any red and white tree that needs even, warm light
picks.skip_if: Your tree came pre-lit with enough lights already
picks.quirky_fact: Wrapping lights along each branch instead of around the outside uses more lights but makes the tree glow from inside.
picks.product_name: Warm White LED Christmas String Lights 66 ft 200 Count

picks.description: A large red velvet bow with long tails is an easy topper for a red and white tree and looks good from every angle. The tails can trail down the tree and connect to ribbon cascades, which pulls the scheme together. Wired velvet bows hold their shape on the top branch, and you can attach them with floral wire or a zip tie. Pick a bow about 12 to 16 inches wide for a seven-foot tree, larger for taller trees. Choose the same red as your ornaments. A bow costs less than most star toppers and is easy to store. Velvet can crush in storage, so pack it loosely with tissue.
picks.best_for: Classic trees that want a simple, soft topper
picks.skip_if: You love a lit star or angel topper with family history
picks.quirky_fact: Long bow tails that run down the tree make a topper look larger than its real size.
picks.product_name: Large Red Velvet Christmas Tree Topper Bow with Tails

picks.breed: Red and White Wood Bead Garland
picks.description: Wood bead garland in red and white adds a light, rustic swag that softens a busy tree. Drape it in loose scallops from branch to branch, or hang short pieces vertically from the top for a modern look. Natural wood beads mixed with red and white painted ones give a Scandinavian or farmhouse feel, and they pair well with the woven hearts above. A seven-foot tree needs about 30 to 40 feet of garland for full scallops. Bead garland is light and unbreakable, and it stores well wound around a piece of cardboard. Painted beads can chip over time. You can also string your own with wood beads and twine as a family craft.
picks.best_for: Rustic, Nordic and farmhouse trees that need extra texture
picks.skip_if: You want a glossy glam tree; wood beads look casual
picks.quirky_fact: Garland swags look most natural when each scallop dips about the same depth around the tree.
picks.product_name: Red and White Wood Bead Garland Christmas Tree Decoration

faqs.question: How many ornaments do I need for a red and white tree?
faqs.answer: A common guide is about 10 ornaments per vertical foot of tree for a full look, so a seven-foot tree takes roughly 70, plus ribbon and picks. Mixed sets of 50 to 100 shatterproof balls cover most of that. Use several sizes, put the biggest deep in the branches, and spread both colors evenly so no side looks mostly red or mostly white.

faqs.question: Should I use a green or white tree for red and white decor?
faqs.answer: A green tree gives the most contrast and the classic candy cane look, because red and white both stand out against dark needles. A flocked or white tree makes the scheme softer and more wintry, with the red doing most of the work. On a white tree, lean toward more red ornaments so the decorations don't disappear into the branches.

faqs.question: What lights go best with a red and white tree?
faqs.answer: Warm white lights suit most red and white trees because they make red look rich and white look creamy. Cool white lights can make white ornaments look blue and red look pink. Avoid multicolor strings, which add green, blue and yellow and break the two-color scheme. Plan about 100 lights per foot of tree height for a well-lit look.

faqs.question: How do I keep a red and white tree from looking like a candy cane?
faqs.answer: Limit stripes to one element, such as ribbon or a few peppermint ornaments, and let the rest be solid colors. Add texture with knit, wood, felt and velvet pieces in the same two colors, which gives a Scandinavian or cottage look instead of a candy shop. A single deep red rather than bright red also makes the tree feel calmer.

faqs.question: Can I add a third color to a red and white tree?
faqs.answer: A metal works best as the third color. Gold or brass warms the scheme, silver keeps it crisp and cool, and natural wood adds a rustic Nordic feel. Keep the extra color to a handful of pieces, such as a few gold balls or wood bead garland, so red and white stay in charge of the tree.

seo_title: Red and White Christmas Tree Ideas 2026: 10 Looks
answer: Start a red and white Christmas tree with a mixed red and white ball ornament set, then add striped ribbon and a buffalo check tree skirt. The deciding factor is balance: roughly equal red and white spread evenly over the tree, with warm white lights, keeps the look crisp instead of patchy.
method: Picked from Pinterest's trending searches for red and white Christmas tree ideas in late October 2026, then ordered by how much each idea shapes the finished tree for its cost and effort, and how many seasons it lasts.
